verdict.rationale: Godot is a local, MIT-licensed engine. Your source assets live directly in your own project folder, imported copies are kept internally under .godot/imported, and you remain sole copyright owner of your content, so leaving carries little lock-in. However, no evidence documents an export of all project data, or that Godot's own scene and resource files use open, readable formats. Missing for 10: documented open/text formats for scenes and resources, an explicit data-export or migration path, independent corroboration of portability.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can export all of my data in open formats and leave

citations.quote: To import assets in Godot, place your assets (image files, scenes, audio files, fonts, etc) directly in the project folder.
Godot will automatically import these files internally and keep the imported resources hidden in a res://.godot/imported/ folder.
Godot Engine's license terms and copyright do not apply to the content you create with it; you are free to license your games how you see best fit, and will be their sole copyright owner(s).
Godot is completely free and open source under the very permissive MIT license.
